title: The bestiary's look is the canonical display for every unit (enemies, friendly, neutral), its stage larger for the appendages, the tiers named Cutis-Soft and Cutis-Core by colour; the units work (pearl-enemies, swarm-lab-pearl, bestiary) merged and made the default branch
context: Owner, 2026-10-14, after opening the terminal: "looking good for the Bestiary, we want that look and feel to become the new canonical display for all units. 2) for all new enemies let's have the 'playground' they are displayed on larger, so that we can see their appendages extending further, that is key. it's ok if they are shown smaller because of that. 3) we need to change the names to adapt. Cutis-Soft Ivory, Cutis-Soft Lemon, Cutis-Soft Sky, etc. for all the colors, then Cutis-Core Pumpkin for orange, Cutis-Core Emerald, etc. for the harder cores. The Bestiary also become the new view for all Friendly units (Tank, Isao, Gunship, both SOL, etc.) and Neutral (the buildings). 4) We merge. everything we worked on with the new units become the new default branch upon which we will build." The day's branches: pearl-enemies (the build-up 2026-10-14-pearl-waves-build-up, the full waves, the --story counts, the bisect records), swarm-lab-pearl (2026-10-14-swarm-lab-pearl-mode and its rounds, the hull contact extracted to src/fx/hull-contact.js), bestiary (2026-10-14-bestiary-terminal-enemies). main was at e4853f55 (2026-10-07) and is an ancestor of pearl-enemies.
outcome: Decided: (1) the terminal's look and feel (the frame, the CRT pass, the card, the live stage) is the canonical display for every unit from here: the friendly units (the tank, Isao, the gunship, SOL-82 and SOL-88, ...) and the neutral buildings become pages of the same terminal (pieces two and three of the bestiary spec, each brainstormed before it is built); (2) the stage is larger: the disc 36 -> 54 m, the lure's loop 15 -> 24 m with its lead 6 -> 9, the pack seated wider, the camera's orbit 34 -> 52 m at 32 m up (src/content/bestiary.js BESTIARY_STAGE), the bodies smaller on screen by the owner's leave; (3) the tiers are named by their core and colour in src/content/pearl-enemies.js PEARL_TIERS (the ids unchanged): Cutis-Soft Ivory (white), Cutis-Soft Lemon (yellow), Cutis-Soft Sky (blue), Cutis-Core Pumpkin (orange), Cutis-Core Emerald (green), Cutis-Core Amethyst (purple), Cutis-Core Umber (brown), Cutis-Core Onyx (black); the three the owner did not spell out (Amethyst, Umber, Onyx) are the executor's picks for him to change; the bestiary's card head is the name without a TIER suffix and its list names are the same; (4) swarm-lab-pearl and bestiary merged into pearl-enemies (the one conflict, docs/STATE.md's two new sections, kept both), main fast-forwarded to it and pushed: the default branch is the merged work. Verified on the merged tree before the push: npm test, npm run check, npm run architecture, and the browser steps --bestiary, --swarm-pearl, --pearl-story, --sectors, --ground-feed, --story and --round6 (results in the session's records). Not merged: refactor-round-2 (cut from pearl-enemies 8bf59188 on 2026-10-13, the owner's playtest pending) and refactor-run (superseded in content by pearl-enemies); both stay as branches for the owner's call.
alternatives: Keep the type names (AMOEBA · PHAGE) as the entries' names and the colours as subtitles: the owner named the tiers themselves; the types stay in the card's data table.
Merge refactor-round-2 with the rest: it is not units work, the owner has not test-run it, and it would need a rebase onto the merged tree first; left for his call.
Scale the bodies up with the stage: the owner accepts them smaller so the appendages' reach reads.
evidence: commits cff72ea5 (names and stage) on bestiary; merges of swarm-lab-pearl and bestiary into pearl-enemies (e5f3bd14); the battery logs in the session scratchpad merge/
src/content/pearl-enemies.js PEARL_TIERS; src/content/bestiary.js BESTIARY_STAGE and ENTRIES; src/domain/bestiary.js the card label; test/bestiary.mjs; scripts/browser-test.mjs --bestiary
